Description: Would bring back a Tenant Advocacy Office to help renters understand and exercise their rights.
Outcome Details: The office remained unfunded after ABC Vancouver voted in 2023 to end it despite a staff recommendation to continue the service.

Description: Would use City-owned land and rezonings to support $10-a-day childcare facilities.
Outcome Details: ABC amended the motion to ask the Province to fund more daycare spaces instead. The original municipal-support proposal did not proceed.

Description: Calls for Vancouver to fund a $25-a-month transit pass for people earning less than $40,000.
Outcome Details: ABC replaced the proposal with a motion to lobby senior governments, which passed unanimously. The City did not create the transit pass.

Description: Sets the city's tax rate, service levels, police funding, and capital priorities for 2025.
Outcome Details: The final budget passed with a 3.9% property-tax increase.

Description: Repeals Vancouver's 25-cent single-use beverage cup fee, reducing a direct cost for customers.
Outcome Details: Council repealed the 25-cent fee, so businesses no longer had to charge it to customers.

Description: Sets the city's tax, policing, service, and infrastructure priorities for the year.
Outcome Details: The final budget passed with a 10.7% property-tax increase; the tax increase was the largest in more than a decade.

Description: Directs staff to prepare a 2026 budget with no property-tax increase.
Outcome Details: The final 2026 operating budget froze property taxes at 2025 levels.

Vote: Allowing Natural Gas in New Construction No. 1
Description: Directs staff to amend the by-law to allow natural gas for heating and hot water in new construction.
Outcome Details: Council directed staff to return before November 1, 2024, with a plan to implement the changes.

Vote: Allowing Natural Gas in New Construction No. 2
Description: Considers a by-law amendment to implement the natural-gas changes proposed in July 2024.
Outcome Details: After more than 140 speakers and significant public opposition, Council did not reverse the natural-gas ban.

Vote: Allowing Natural Gas in New Construction No. 3
Description: Changes building policy to allow natural gas in new construction on affordability grounds.
Outcome Details: Council approved the change, reversing the previous natural-gas restriction. The decision also ended greenhouse-gas reporting under Energize Vancouver.

Description: Repeals Vancouver's 25-cent single-use beverage cup fee, reducing a direct cost for customers.
Outcome Details: Council repealed the 25-cent fee, removing an incentive to avoid disposable beverage cups.

Description: Approves a zero-means-zero budget that increases the police budget and makes substantial cuts elsewhere.
Outcome Details: The budget cut $8.3 million from energy-retrofit programs and substantially reduced staffing for sustainability work.

Description: Directs the City to increase its supply of climate-smart renewable energy.
Outcome Details: Council passed the motion, but later decisions allowing natural gas in new buildings limited its practical effect.

Description: Directs action to improve climate resilience and reduce emissions in existing multifamily buildings.
Outcome Details: Council passed the motion and launched a funding program to help retrofit older apartment buildings.

Description: Directs staff to accelerate climate measures, including support for active transportation, electric vehicles, and heat pumps.
Outcome Details: Council passed the motion, setting early direction for climate action. Later ABC policy decisions paused or reversed much of the proposed work.

Description: Temporarily pauses new and ongoing Integrity Commissioner investigations while Council reviews the office's scope and mandate.
Outcome Details: Council later backed down and allowed the commissioner's work to resume in late 2024.

Description: Begins transferring parks and recreation governance from the elected Park Board to Council.
Outcome Details: Province didn't follow through with Ken Sim's request to abolish the Park Board.

Description: Adopts direct structural safeguards protecting the Integrity Commissioner from political interference, including protections recommended by Reece Harding's independent review.
Outcome Details: ABC used a strike-and-replace amendment to direct staff to study the recommendations instead of immediately adopting the safeguards.

Description: Directs staff to examine whether the city could use, hold, or accept Bitcoin.
Outcome Details: Council approved a staff examination of possible Bitcoin use. The City did not invest in Bitcoin.

Vote: Sanctioning Mayor Sim for Integrity Violation
Description: Deciding whether to sanction Mayor Ken Sim after an independent investigation found that he misused the influence of his office and harassed Councillor Sean Orr.
Outcome Details: Council imposed no sanctions and did not require an apology; the ABC majority questioned the investigation, while Mayor Sim was absent for a conflict of interest.

Vote: Sanctioning Cllr Boyle for Integrity Violation
Description: Deciding whether to sanction Councillor Christine Boyle after she disparaged the mayor's chief of staff.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously endorsed the Integrity Commissioner’s recommended sanctions.

Description: Requires public disclosure of total compensation received by Council members from taxpayer-funded and external sources.
Outcome Details: The City added an open-data source listing the mayor and councillors total compensation.

Description: Creates a pilot program using public performance tracking and regular review meetings to improve City-service accountability.
Outcome Details: Monthly meetings are diving into statistics to look for systematic problems in the city.

Description: Would transform 17 small commercial nodes across the city into walkable, mixed-use community hubs.
Outcome Details: Council did not approve the full plan. It adopted only minor Official Development Plan changes and space-efficient stair amendments.

Description: Would replace site-specific rezonings with citywide zoning for mixed-income social, supportive, and co-operative housing.
Outcome Details: Council defeated the proposal, originally advanced by OneCity Councillor Christine Boyle. The citywide zoning approach did not proceed.

Description: Decides whether to continue funding the City Renter Office, which provided tenant-rights support at an annual cost of $600,000.
Outcome Details: Council passed a last-minute ABC amendment to end the City Renter Office, despite a staff recommendation to continue it. The office closed, ending the City-run tenant-rights service.

Description: Push to restore the city’s tenant advocacy office after ABC closed it in 2023
Outcome Details: A tie-vote means that renters continue to lack support at Vancouver City Hall.

Description: Directs staff to renew or extend temporary modular-housing leases, find longer-term sites, and avoid a net loss of supportive-housing units while permanent housing is built.
Outcome Details: Council did not extend the leases, and 98 downtown housing units closed to make room for a planned Vancouver Art Gallery project. The gallery project later did not proceed.

Description: Keeps the Empty Homes Tax at 3% rather than increasing it to 5%.
Outcome Details: Council approved the report-back motion without increasing the Empty Homes Tax to 5%; the higher rate would have generated an estimated $20 million annually for affordable housing.

Description: Would allow shops and apartments in Shaughnessy, one of Vancouver most exclusively zoned neighbourhoods.
Outcome Details: Shaughnessy remained largely exclusive despite a long-term decline in its population.

Description: Pauses city contributions of land or funding for net-new supportive housing.
Outcome Details: Vancouver has refused to add social housing since 2025. The pause was advertised as temporary, but a motion by Bligh in 2026 to reverse the ban was defeated by ABC.

Description: Motion to give renters across Vanvouver the same protections that exist within the Broadway Plan.
Outcome Details: Renters outside of the Broadway area have weaker tenant protections.

Description: Allows multiplexes in more neighbourhoods with a modest increase in density.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved the zoning changes, allowing the incremental multiplex proposal to proceed.

Description: 3 rental towers with more than 1,000 homes beside Commercial-Broadway Station, amid major affordability and scale concerns.
Outcome Details: After nearly a decade of proposals, pushback and debate, the megatowers are finally approved.

Vote: Social Housing Near Italian Cultural Centre
Description: Approves a six-storey social-housing building with 64 homes near the Italian Cultural Centre.
Outcome Details: Despite approximately 100 people speaking out against the proposal, council approved it.

Description: Intended to increase family-friendly density near under-utilized schools and seek out opportunities to work with the Vancouver School Board.
Outcome Details: Council approved the motion. Its approach was later incorporated into the Villages Plan, which faced significant opposition to density near underenrolled Dunbar schools.

Description: Approves a 17-storey, 170-home rental tower at 2156-2174 West 14th Avenue under the Broadway Plan.
Outcome Details: Council approved the rental tower. It was one of nine Broadway Plan towers, with nearly 1,500 rental homes, approved within a few months.

Vote: Right to Cooling for Strata Buildings
Description: Considers giving residents of strata buildings the right to install air conditioning.
Outcome Details: Residents of strata buildings can move forward with measures to install air conditioning.

Description: Changes zoning and related policies to accelerate SRO replacement, increase social housing, and create a $5 million Downtown Eastside Housing Revitalization Grant Program.
Outcome Details: The zoning and related policy changes proceeded after amendments to protect existing SROs failed.

Description: Approves a multi-block downtown redevelopment with three high-rise towers, a 920-room hotel, commercial space, and a linked 237-unit social-housing project at 388 Abbott Street.
Outcome Details: Council approved the rezoning 7–3; Rebecca Bligh was absent, and Pete Fry, Lucy Maloney, and Sean Orr opposed.

Description: Adds $2.64 million to the VPD budget, including ongoing and one-time funding for full implementation of body-worn cameras, plus related investigative and risk-management costs.
Outcome Details: Council approved the amendment as part of the 2025 budget.

Description: Would lower the speed limit to 30 or 40 km/h on selected downtown roadways with high pedestrian activity.
Outcome Details: Council did not lower the proposed speed limits. An ABC amendment removed them from the plan.

Description: Seeks additional red-light and speed cameras in Vancouver to reduce crashes.
Outcome Details: Council did not enact the original motion. ABC used a strike-and-replace amendment to request a staff study instead.

Vote: Safe Streets for Trick or Treat
Description: Considers simpler, safer temporary street closures for Halloween block parties.
Outcome Details: ABC used a strike-and-replace to refer this to staff for more study.

Description: Considers a lower speed limit on Cornwall Avenue following a severe crash involving a child near Kitsilano Beach.
Outcome Details: Council amended the proposed 30 km/h limit to 40 km/h and passed the amended motion. The corridor received a smaller speed reduction than originally proposed.

Description: Directs the City not to enforce the indoor-smoking prohibition for Health Canada-approved supervised-consumption sites that meet WorkSafeBC requirements, enabling supervised inhalation services.
Outcome Details: Council adopted the resolution unanimously. It applied for two years and directed staff to evaluate the spaces and report back.

Description: Approves a $2.1 million VPD budget increase and a one-time $11.2 million reallocation to address forecasted police-budget deficits.
Outcome Details: The final components passed with some councillors abstaining.

Description: Approves Vancouver Vision Zero Safe Mobility Plan to reduce traffic-related fatalities.
Outcome Details: Council approved the plan, establishing a shared City Hall commitment to reduce traffic-related deaths.

Description: Asks senior governments to address increasingly bright vehicle headlights.
Outcome Details: Council approved the motion, but federal action is required to change national vehicle-lighting rules.

Description: Allows VPD access to city traffic cameras, raising major privacy and surveillance questions.
Outcome Details: Police can access traffic-camera feeds without a warrant, expanding police surveillance access.

Description: Directs staff to use all lawful city tools to prevent the opening of a proposed overdose prevention site at 900 Helmcken Street.
Outcome Details: Province ultimately cancelled the project in August 2026.

Description: Approves funding to hire 100 police officers, part of ABC promise to hire 100 police officers and 100 nurses.
Outcome Details: 12% increase to police budget, including $8.0 million for enabling hiring.

Description: City Staff gave council two options for the Broadway street design - one with active transportation lanes and one without.
Outcome Details: Council adopted a Broadway design without active-transportation lanes. The requested bike-lane option was not included.

Description: Restores two-way vehicle traffic on Beach Avenue near Stanley Park instead of maintaining an all-ages-and-abilities bike route.
Outcome Details: Council sought to remove the Beach Avenue bike lane, but the Park Board retained it.

Description: Shifts rapid-transit planning focus from the 41st/49th Avenue corridor to the Hastings Street corridor.
Outcome Details: Council endorsed the shift to focus on Hastings. The 41st and 49th Avenue routes remained the region second- and third-busiest bus routes, while the R5 on Hastings ranked tenth.

Description: Asks senior governments to support a fare-free transit route pilot in Vancouver.
Outcome Details: Council did not endorse the pilot. It would have required support from TransLink and the Province.

Vote: Priority Snow Removal on Transit Routes
Description: Considers prioritizing snow clearing on routes heavily used by buses.
Outcome Details: Snow and ice removal at transit trouble spots was not prioritized under the motion.

Description: Directs staff to redesign the bike lane near Vancouver General Hospital, considering a bi-directional bike lane on the north side.
Outcome Details: After killing the idea of a bike lane on Broadway, ABC directed city staff to spend up to $20 million changing the design near the hospital.

Description: Authorizes Vancouver's first shared e-scooter program.
Outcome Details: Council approved the pilot, enabling shared Lime e-scooters to operate in Vancouver.

Vote: Dedicated Bus Lanes on Priority Routes
Description: Commits the city to adding 9 new priority bus lanes, at a rate of 2 per year. Corridors include: Main Street / Kingsway, 49th Ave, Marine Drive, and Hastings Street.
Outcome Details: Despite passing unanimously, no new bus lanes have been added yet. 49th Ave should open in 2027 but Hastings has been paused.

Description: Expands school travel planning to help more children walk, cycle, and roll to school.
Outcome Details: The program currently serves four schools per year and is expected to expand. A separate proposal to double or triple the current rate failed.

Vote: Safer Slower Streets: 30 km/h Speed Limits
Description: Approves a phased program to lower local-street speeds to 30 km/h.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved a phased program to introduce 30 km/h neighbourhood slow zones, beginning in 25 neighbourhoods.

Description: Reaffirms support for extending rapid transit from UBC to the Millennium Line.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously called for the Broadway SkyTrain extension to UBC to be accelerated.

Description: Directs staff to study restricting right turns on red where they conflict with pedestrian and cycling movements.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously directed staff to assess right-turn-on-red restrictions at high-risk intersections.

Description: Advances a transformative active-transportation pathway in South Vancouver.
Outcome Details: Staff are now exploring a 9 km Greenway along the railway from Marine Drive Station to the River District.

Description: Would transform 17 small commercial nodes across the city into walkable, mixed-use community hubs.
Outcome Details: Council did not approve the full plan. It adopted only minor Official Development Plan changes and space-efficient stair amendments.

Description: Considers a rezoning for a 25-storey hotel with restaurant space at 2028–2038 Barclay Street in the West End.
Outcome Details: Council referred the proposal back to staff for redesign with the developer. The rezoning was not approved as proposed.

Description: Considers a 30-year plan to redesign and protect 90 acres of coastal parks, beaches, and street networks between the Burrard Bridge and Stanley Park.
Outcome Details: Council ended the plan, citing concerns about the estimated $300 million cost of the 30-year revitalization project.

Description: Reduces the scope of the Water Street pedestrian program to summer Sundays after the larger 2024 pilot.
Outcome Details: In October 2024, Council decided to reduce the pedestrian zones to weekends only. Then, they further reduced it to Sundays only.

Description: Extends a pedestrianized Granville Street pilot beyond the FIFA World Cup period.
Outcome Details: Council approved $4.75 million to keep the Granville Street pedestrian zone in place for seven weeks.

Description: Amends zoning to permit a 250-room floating hotel, new dock, public walkway, and commercial uses beside the Vancouver Convention Centre.
Outcome Details: Council approved the zoning changes, allowing the floating hotel project to proceed toward a planned 2027 opening.

Description: Removes required minimum off-street parking in major west-side areas.
Outcome Details: Minimum general-purpose parking requirements were removed for new developments in the West End and Broadway Plan areas. Accessible, visitor, bicycle, and loading spaces remained required.

Description: Eliminates mandatory minimum parking requirements for new development citywide.
Outcome Details: Council passed the measure. 6 months after removing parking minimums in the West End, Council eliminated minimum general-purpose parking requirements citywide.

Description: Adopts Vancouver's long-term citywide land-use framework, guiding where housing, jobs, transportation, parks, and infrastructure can grow over the next 30 years.
Outcome Details: The plan establishes a framework for the next 30 years of growth, but does not change zoning on its own.

Description: Approves a crossing where pedestrians can move through the intersection in every direction.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved a Granville–Robson pedestrian-scramble pilot and requested a follow-up report.

Description: Tests a more pedestrian-oriented, car-free Water Street in Gastown.
Outcome Details: Council approved the July–August 2024 Gastown pedestrian-zone pilot; the amendment was defeated.

Description: Approves a rezoning that makes space for a three-storey school serving 630 students.
Outcome Details: After more than 20 years of planning, the rezoning cleared the way for a new Olympic Village school expected in 2029.

Description: Provides $30,000 in emergency funding for Car Free festivals on Commerical and Main.
Outcome Details: Emergency funding allowed the Car-Free Day festivals to proceed.
